claim: Daily 70 µg (2800 IU) Vitamin D3 supplementation for 12 weeks significantly raised serum 25(OH)D from 33 nmol/L to 90 nmol/L in postmenopausal women with vitamin D insufficiency.
stance_target: D3 supplementation effectively corrects vitamin D insufficiency
scope_conditions: RCT, n=76 postmenopausal women, 25(OH)D <50 nmol/L at baseline, wintertime, latitude 56°N Denmark, 12 weeks
quoted_support: At the end of the study, the levels of 25(OH) had increased significantly to 90 nmol/L (95%, CI: 86 to 95) in the vitamin D group as compared with 30 nmol/L (95% CI: 28 to 33) in the control group.

claim: Moderately high daily Vitamin D3 (2800 IU) significantly increased serum carnitine, choline, and urea — markers associated with muscle catabolism — suggesting potential skeletal muscle harm.
stance_target: high-dose D3 supplementation may have adverse muscle effects
scope_conditions: RCT secondary metabolomics analysis, postmenopausal women with D insufficiency, 12 weeks, 2800 IU/day
quoted_support: Vitamin D supplementation significantly increased the serum levels of carnitine to 6.0 µmol/L (95% CI: −1.1 to 13) vs. −5.5 µmol/L (−13 to 2.0), p=0.03), choline to −0.00 µmol/L (−2.2 to 2.1) vs. −4.1 µmol/L (−6.7 to −1.6), p=0.02), and urea to 45 µmol/L (24 to 66 vs. 13 µmol/L (−7.0 to 34, p=0.03).

claim: Detrimental effects on muscle health from D3 supplementation are not reported at dosages below 20 µg/day (800 IU); adverse effects emerge at 70 µg/day (2800 IU) and above.
stance_target: 2000 IU D3 daily is safe for muscle health; harm is dose-dependent at higher levels
scope_conditions: Based on review of available RCT literature, authors' assessment
quoted_support: Detrimental effects on muscle health are not reported with dosages below 20 µg/day. In contrast, dosages at 70 µg/day are commonly used to treat insufficiency.

claim: Increases in carnitine, choline, creatinine, and urea from D3 supplementation negatively correlated with muscle strength and physical performance outcomes.
stance_target: elevated muscle catabolism markers from high-dose D3 correspond to functional muscle decline
scope_conditions: Secondary correlational analysis of RCT, n=76, TUG test, handgrip strength, knee flexion 60°
quoted_support: Changes in the levels of carnitine (r = 0.29, p = 0.01), choline (r = 0.23, p = 0.04), and urea (r = 0.26, p = 0.02) correlated positively with changes in the TUG test, i.e., increases in these metabolites were associated with a longer time spent on performing the test.
